answer: Submissions that land within 187 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The quartz detector writes to ripple, and ivory shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, and as a result the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 77 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 2 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
